title: Drop-downs, Checkboxes & Validation
goal: Stop bad data at the door with drop-down lists, checkboxes and number or date limits, and count the results reliably.

steps.text:
Five tasks, and every one of them is finished. But the count says only **3**.

One person typed “Complete”, another typed “Dne”. Excel counts only the exact word **Done**.

**Data validation** stops this at the door: a cell accepts only what you allow, usually through a **drop-down list**. Press the button to see the count after one cell is fixed.

steps.prompt:
Validation rules apply to the cells you select **first**. Select the Status cells of the four parcels.

Click ==B2==, drag down to ==B5==, then press [[Enter]].
steps.wrongFeedback: The Status cells are `B2` to `B5`. Leave out the header, and the Allowed list in column D.
clues: Drag from the first empty Status cell to the last.

steps.prompt:
Tap [[Alt]], [[A]], [[V]], [[V]] one after another: Data → Data Validation → Data Validation.

In the box, set **Allow** to **List**, and **Source** to the three words in column D: `=$D$2:$D$4` (or type `Pending,Shipped,Delivered`). Keep **In-cell dropdown** ticked and press OK. On a Mac, use the Data tab → Data Validation.
clues: Alt, A, V, V: tap each key, one after another.

steps.prompt:
The list is ready. A drop-down lets you click a word; our sheet makes you type it, but only words from the list in column D.

Use the notes to fill ==B2:B5==, then check each word is spelled exactly like the list.
steps.explain: Every status is now one of three exact words. That's why a count of “Delivered” will be right: 2 here, no typos hiding.
clues: “Arrived” and “Handed over” mean the same allowed word.
Use [[Enter]] to move down after each one.

wrongFeedback.wrongValue: Use only the three words in column D: Pending, Shipped, Delivered. Arrived or handed over means the parcel is **Delivered**; left the shop means **Shipped**; not collected yet means **Pending**.

steps.topic: Open the list with the keyboard
steps.prompt:
You're on a cell that has a drop-down. Press [[Alt]] + [[↓]] and the list opens. Use the arrow keys to choose, then [[Enter]].

Same on a Mac: [[Option]] + [[↓]].
clues: Hold Alt and press the Down arrow.

steps.prompt:
A **checkbox** is a drop-down's cousin. Select cells, then Insert tab → **Checkbox** (recent Microsoft 365 only).

A ticked box holds the value **TRUE**; an empty one holds **FALSE**. Toggle one from the keyboard: click ==B4== (Charger) and press [[Space]].
clues: Select the Charger cell, then press the space bar.

steps.prompt:
Because a tick is just TRUE, you can count ticks like any value.

Charger is packed now. In ==B8== count how many items are ticked.
steps.explain: **5**: only Sunscreen is still FALSE. Counting `TRUE` gives you a live progress count that rises with every tick.

wrongFeedback.wrongValue: Count only the ticked boxes, which hold TRUE. Don't count all six rows.
wrongFeedback.missingFunction: Use a function that counts cells matching a condition.

clues: Count the cells in `B2:B7` equal to `TRUE`.

steps.prompt:
Another rule: **Whole number between 1 and 5**, so ratings can't be silly. Excel refuses anything that breaks it.

These guests were typed one after another. Click the **first** entry Excel would have refused, then press [[Enter]].
steps.wrongFeedback: `B5` (the 7) is also refused, but look earlier. “Whole number” means no decimals, so Chitra's 2.5 fails first.
clues: Whole numbers have nothing after the decimal point.

steps.prompt:
A hotel's check-in column allows **dates on or after today** (15 Jan 2026) only.

In ==C2== test whether Asha's date in `B2` would be accepted: TRUE or FALSE.
steps.explain: **TRUE**: Asha's date is exactly today, and “on or after” includes it. Ben's 10 Jan would be refused. In Data Validation that's Allow: **Date**, Data: **greater than or equal to**.

wrongFeedback.wrongValue: “On or after today” includes today. Use `>=`, not `>`.

steps.prompt:
Your supplier list is mostly fixed, but a **new supplier** turns up now and then. Staff should be warned that the name isn't on the list, and be allowed to continue if they're sure.

Which **Error Alert** style fits?
steps.explain: **Stop** blocks the entry completely. **Warning** says “This isn't on the list. Continue?” and lets them choose Yes. **Information** only tells them and doesn't ask. Add an **Input Message** too: a small note that appears when the cell is selected, like “Pick from the list”.
wrongFeedback: Stop never lets them continue. That's right for IDs or ratings, but too strict here.
Information just informs and accepts the entry. It doesn't ask the user to confirm.
clues: Which style asks the person whether to continue?

steps.prompt:
You add a Status drop-down to a column that **already** has “Dne” and “Complete” typed in.

What happens to those old entries?
options: Excel corrects them to the nearest list item
Nothing: they stay, because validation only checks new typing
steps.explain: Validation only checks what's typed **after** the rule exists, and it doesn't check pasted values at all. To find old bad entries use Data Validation → **Circle Invalid Data**.
wrongFeedback: Excel never guesses. It leaves existing values untouched.
Nothing is deleted. The old values just sit there, unchecked.
clues: When does Excel check a cell against the rule?

steps.prompt: This to-do list uses checkboxes. How many tasks are **still not ticked**? Put the answer in ==B8==.
steps.explain: **4**: Book, Pay, Call and Email are FALSE. Only 2 tasks are ticked, so don't mix up which value you're counting.

wrongFeedback.parseError: Check the brackets and the comma.
wrongFeedback.wrongValue: Count the unticked boxes: the cells holding FALSE.
